minutes.headline: Board voted to treat tax bills as mailed January 6 (May 1 due date), pending Town Counsel confirming DOR allows it.
minutes.summary: The meeting centered on the FY23 tax bill mailing-date dispute and the abatement controversy, with heavy public and board criticism of the Board of Assessors. The board also approved a pole relocation, a Council on Aging appointment, the Nashoba dispatch agreement, ARPA spending, and reviewed FY24 capital and warrant articles. It then went into executive session.

public_comment.topic: Criticized oversight of the tax assessment and the town manager's supervision of the principal assessor; demanded answers.
Asked how the 135 percent increase on lakefront properties was calculated and urged the board to get that information before abatements are denied.
Objected to the pole relocation: outdated plan on file, drainage trench, school bus stop and traffic concerns.
Resident warned that bears are raiding bird feeders.
Asked whether anyone can file an abatement after the cutoff given the mailing date vote.
Questioned why the sewer department with large retained earnings is seeking ARPA funds.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to treat FY23 tax bills as mailed in January, making May 1 the due date, once Town Counsel hears from the state Department of Revenue.
The board approved committing ARPA funds to public safety building security cameras and to help the Board of Assessors with assessment services.
The board accepted the updated Nashoba Valley Regional Dispatch District agreement, 3-0 with one recusal.
The board approved the Howard Street pole relocation after a resident objected to the plan, and accepted Town Counsel's response to an open meeting law complaint.
The board reviewed FY24 capital and warrant articles, deferring recommendations to next week, then entered executive session.

why_it_matters: The mailing-date vote decides whether the abatement filing window has closed, which affects residents contesting their assessments, especially lakefront owners who raised concerns at the meeting.
ARPA money is being used for assessment services and building security, and the FY24 capital plan and warrant articles drawing on stabilization and free cash will go to a town meeting vote.
watch_next: Town Counsel's confirmation that the Department of Revenue allows the January mailing date, on which the vote depends.
Next week's meeting, where the town manager presents budget and capital numbers and the board makes recommendations, and the Board of Assessors is again invited.
